    AI Overview
    As of
    April 2, 2026, major upcoming launches include multiple SpaceX Starlink missions from Florida and California, alongside the historic crewed Artemis II Moon mission. Key launches include Starlink 10-58 from Cape Canaveral and Starlink 17-35 from Vandenberg, with further missions scheduled for early April. 
    Upcoming Rocket Launches (Subject to Change) 
    • April 2, 2026 - SpaceX Starlink 10-58
      • Rocket: Falcon 9
      • Location: Launch Complex 40, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, FL
      • Time: 7:52 a.m. – 11:52 p.m. EDT
    • April 2, 2026 - SpaceX Starlink 17-35
      • Rocket: Falcon 9
      • Location: Space Launch Complex 4E, Vandenberg Space Force Base, CA
      • Time: 4:03 p.m. – 8:03 p.m. PT
    • April 2, 2026 - Space Pioneer Tianlong-3 (Demo)
      • Location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, China
    • April 8, 2026 - Northrop Grumman CRS-24
      • Rocket: SpaceX Falcon 9
      • Location: Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, FL
    • TBA - ULA Atlas V (Amazon Leo 5)
      • Location: Launch Complex 41, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, FL
    • TBA - ULA Vulcan Centaur (Amazon Leo-Vulcan Leo 1)
      • Location: Space Coast, FL 
    Highlighted Missions 
    • Artemis II: NASA's crewed flight around the Moon is in the immediate queue for April 2026, marking a significant milestone in the Artemis program.
    • SpaceX Starlink: Continues to launch frequent batches of satellites for its internet constellation from both East and West coasts. 
    For real-time updates and live coverage, monitor the FLORIDA TODAY Space Team, Spaceflight Now, or SpaceX's official launch page.

    When will you see it? Check out the map. It shows how many seconds after liftoff different places will have to wait to see the rocket in the sky (in 10-second increments). For example, Jacksonville residents will need to look southeast while Miami residents will need to look north & Tampa folks look generally east.
